reason: This study aims to compare the recording of infant sleep environment details, specifically focusing on sleeping arrangements, between the NCFRP case series and PRAMS population reference surveys. The rationale is that while there may be heterogeneity in ascertainment and reporting of sleep environments in case-report systems (as noted by prior work), no direct comparison has been made between these specific data sources to understand how such details are recorded differently. This gap is important because discrepancies in recording can lead to biased comparisons when using these datasets for research or public health practice.
